title: Parliament debates Budget 2026
what_it_is: A parliamentary debate on Budget 2026, with MPs speaking and the Prime Minister responding to clarifications.
why_it_matters: MPs said Budget 2026 continues one-off support such as CDC vouchers and utilities rebates, and strengthens CPF top-ups and higher contribution rates for seniors. They also said it raises the monthly household income threshold for student care fee assistance to $6,500 and lowers PARF rebates by 45% with a $30,000 cap. The transcript records many further proposals, but does not state that they have been adopted.

key_points.point: Cost of living remains the top concern from public engagements.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: Cost of living remains the top concern.

key_points.point: Suggests reviewing the $20,000 income tax exemption threshold.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: I hope the Ministry could consider reviewing whether the $20,000 exemption threshold remains aligned with its original purpose

key_points.point: The Workers' Party supports Budget 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: the WP supports Budget 2026.

key_points.point: Proposes retaining the $500 CDC voucher base for households of three or fewer and adding $150 per person for larger owner-occupied households.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: Retain the $500 base for all households of three members or fewer.

key_points.point: Calls for a report card on the Jobs-Skills Integrator initiative.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) should present a report card on the Jobs-Skills Integrator initiative announced at Budget 2023.

key_points.point: Proposes AI-centric development as the default for new Government services.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
key_points.quote: I propose that this becomes the default methodology for all new Government services

key_points.point: Says the Direct School Admission scheme has become an uneven education battleground.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
key_points.quote: the DSA scheme is now just an uneven battleground in the education arms race

key_points.point: Proposes childcare leave based on number of children, paid caregiving leave and enforceable flexible work arrangements.
key_points.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan
key_points.quote: including childcare leave based on number of children, introducing paid caregiving leave and upgrading Flexible Work Arrangements guidelines to enforceable legislation.

key_points.point: Says AI is moving from tool to operator.
key_points.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
key_points.quote: AI is moving from tool to operator.

key_points.point: Asks the Government to track and release annual AI value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes.
key_points.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
key_points.quote: will the Government commit to tracking and releasing annual value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes attributable to AI adoption across key sectors

key_points.point: Calls for dental care to be integrated into Healthier SG.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: I call for dental care to be integrated into Healthier SG.

key_points.point: Notes PARF rebates have been lowered by 45% and the maximum rebate reduced from $60,000 to $30,000.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: rebates have now been lowered by 45% across the board and the maximum rebate has been reduced from $60,000 to $30,000

key_points.point: Renews call to extend Personal Learning Devices to primary school students.
key_points.speaker: Mr Darryl David
key_points.quote: I would like to renew my call to the Government to make that decision to extend PLDs to primary school students.

key_points.point: Calls for a review of the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme income threshold.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
key_points.quote: it is timely for the Government to review this income threshold

key_points.point: NTUC launched AI-Ready SG to train and upskill workers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
key_points.quote: NTUC has launched "AI-Ready SG", a one-stop platform that will help train and upskill workers to be AI-ready

key_points.point: Says persistent government surpluses are private sector deficits.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: Persistent government surpluses are, by definition, private sector deficits.

key_points.point: Calls for bringing back estate duty.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: we must seriously consider bringing back estate duty

key_points.point: Speaks for the unemployed, underemployed, under-represented, untrained and under-served.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: I call them the "5 U's" – the unemployed, the underemployed, the under-represented, the untrained and the under-served.

key_points.point: Calls for advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications to unions and the Government.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: introducing advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications (MRNs) to unions and the Government can provide more timely and early intervention.

key_points.point: Asks whether there has been agreement with SNEF on advanced retrenchment notifications.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: has there been agreement with SNEF on this particular point?

key_points.point: Says there are tripartite negotiations on the point.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: there are tripartite negotiations on this point.

key_points.point: Says the Government will continually review and strengthen support mechanisms.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: We will continually review and strengthen our support mechanisms.

key_points.point: Says the Government's approach on marriage, procreation, parenthood, adoption and immigration will be shared by Minister Indranee during the COS.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: our approach, as Minister Indranee will share during the COS, will not – of course, marriage, procreation, parenthood within Singapore is important, but also other areas, like adoption, as well as immigration will come in as well.

key_points.point: Says Singapore has consistently performed better than expected.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: we have consistently performed better than expected.

key_points.point: Says human capacity and human capital are critical.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: human capacity, human capital is critical.

key_points.point: Says the Government will take care of retirees.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: we will take care of our retirees.

key_points.point: Says the Government will help young seniors.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: we will certainly help our young seniors.

key_points.point: Says the fundamentals are to keep growth and keep the economy growing.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
key_points.quote: keep growth, keep our economy growing

what_happens_next: Several Members said they would raise details at the Committee of Supply debates; the Prime Minister said Minister Indranee will share the Government's approach on marriage, procreation, parenthood, adoption and immigration during the COS.
not_said: Whether the Government will adopt the proposed changes to CDC voucher distribution.
Whether the $20,000 income tax exemption threshold will be reviewed or adjusted.
Whether the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme income threshold will be raised.
Whether advance retrenchment notification will be agreed by the tripartite partners.
Whether transitional relief will be provided for car buyers affected by the PARF rebate changes.
Whether dental care will be integrated into Healthier SG.
Whether Personal Learning Devices will be extended to primary school students.
Whether estate duty or a Net Annual Value tax will be reintroduced.
Whether the Government will commit to annual reporting of AI value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes.
Whether adoption leave will be aligned with maternity leave at 16 weeks.
Whether the Silver Support per capita household income criterion will be removed or reviewed.
Whether the Government will increase subsidies for assisted reproductive treatments.
